reproduced_root_cause: n8n 2.14.1 httpRequest with fullResponse:false unwraps a JSON-array response into one item per element, so a valid empty HPD contacts response ([]) emitted ZERO items. The connection never fired, N09 and all downstream nodes had no runData, and the execution still reported status success -- a zero-item edge indistinguishable from a completed pilot. The fixture harness missed it because it invoked N09 directly with [], the one shape the runtime never produces.

The sentinel carries the spine through empty fan-outs to an explicit terminal artifact. A valid empty contact result continues through the approved seed-roster path -- no invented prospects, no hard-coded offset, no cursor mutation. open_item_for_next_pilot: NIT-1, pre-existing (introduced in PR #7, NOT by this branch), latent today, worth fixing before the next real-data pilot: N08 requests contacts for chunks of 200 registration ids with $limit=2000. Live HPD holds registrations whose contact-row counts exceed that alone (911741: 8688 rows; 911715: 2325 rows, reachable at frame offset ~58400 of 510 pages), so such a chunk would silently truncate and the other 199 registrations in it would lose their contacts with no error. The loss is strictly in the DISCOVERY direction -- a dropped organization produces no candidate, no ledger row and no burn, and a partially framed one keeps portfolio_units >= 3 and non-empty operating_boros so it cannot reach the 3650-day cell. It is also not the D4 class: N08 still emits one envelope per request and the run still reaches its terminal artifact. Suggested fix: raise $limit to SODA's 50000 ceiling AND assert body.length < limit in sodaRows so a truncated page is named rather than inferred. Sampled offsets 0/4000/8000/20000/40000 are all well under 2000 today.
